items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1957-04-11
items.q: The interviewer addresses the interviewee as 'Bill' ('Isn't that right, Bill?'), but the interviewee (Edmond Hall) does not confirm this identity nor does he mention a person named Bill Russell in his responses. The name 'Bill' in the transcript refers to the interviewer or a third party mentioned b

ctx.x: I think it was Thomas Valentine, the trumpet player. We had a drummer by the name of Lionel, I don't know what his last name is, man. The Creole name? No, I don't think so. Is he Lionel Thomas? I can't think of his name.
It might be the fellow who's working with Billy and the Dee, Bill, what's his last name? I forget it.
He used to work with an old time band around Reserve by the name of Dejon.

items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1958-07-18
items.q: [INTERVIEWEE] Well, thank you, Bill. It was a pleasure to do it.

ctx.x: Sure. Sure glad to see you then, all right? Well, we don't want to keep you any longer. I'll turn this off and thank you again.
Well, thank you, Bill. It was a pleasure to do it.

I know a lot of other people will hear this and if possible, we'll get this in print someday, part of this interview. Okay. At least, I mean, we'll fix it up, you know, just take certain parts. Go ahead. Certain parts, sure. Sure. So we've got a few pages of good advice to students and people that want to learn. Now, so many people have heard you on record, but they don't know exactly how you play and your ideas on the music. And as I say, someday, none of us are going to live forever. That'll be lost if we don't…
